keyTakeaways: QLab displays styled subtitle text with Text cues; a Video License and a correctly configured Stage are required.
QLab does not natively import XLSX subtitle sheets in one click, but AppleScript or another importer can turn structured Excel, CSV, or TXT data into cues.
A Pockitle Cue Editor QLab Projection Pack is an offline projection handoff; it does not deploy a show or publish to Viewer.
Pockitle Cue Station can place prepared cues in QLab and follow them for Mac projection; audience-phone sync has separate connection requirements.

faq.question: Can QLab display subtitles?
faq.answer: Yes. Text cues render styled text through QLab's video system and can be assigned to a configured projection Stage.

faq.question: Does QLab natively import an Excel subtitle file?
faq.answer: Not as a one-click XLSX subtitle import. A script or importer can read structured spreadsheet, CSV, or TXT data and create QLab Text cues.

faq.question: Does an Editor QLab Projection Pack sync Viewer?
faq.answer: No. The Editor-origin pack is an offline QLab projection handoff. A deployed show can use Pockitle Cue Station for QLab follow and, when connected, audience-phone subtitles; a separate browser ASM bridge beta is also documented.

faq.question: Can Pockitle Cue Station follow QLab cues?
faq.answer: Yes. After the deployed show is synced and the local receiver and QLab permissions are ready, QLab can advance Station projection. Audience phones also require internet and valid Cloud control.

glossary.definition: A QLab cue that renders styled text as video output.
A Pockitle Cue export containing a static importer, cue data, operator instructions, and supporting files for QLab.
A non-secret Pockitle Cue identity used to update the matching caption Group across revised imports.
A Mac app that can prepare QLab cues and follow them for local projection and, when connected, audience-phone subtitles.
The operator surface that must be open, unlocked, connected, Viewer-ready, and armed before accepting QLab control.
